claims.text: The browser parses the HTML it receives into the DOM, a tree of node objects (elements and text) in memory that mirrors the nesting of the tags.
claims.source_hint: MDN: Introduction to the DOM; HTML spec parsing

claims.text: The browser renders the page from the DOM (plus CSS); JavaScript can find, read, change, add and remove DOM nodes, and those changes appear on screen without a new request.
claims.source_hint: MDN: Introduction to the DOM; Document.querySelector; Node.appendChild

claims.text: View page source shows the HTML as received, not the current DOM; browser developer tools (Elements/Inspector) show the live DOM.
claims.source_hint: Chrome DevTools / Firefox Inspector docs; MDN view-source

claims.text: Reloading a page discards the current DOM and builds a new one from the freshly received HTML.
claims.source_hint: HTML spec: navigation creates a new Document

claims.text: www/index.html has no script; under body it has nine elements: h1, p, ul, three li and three a.
Editing an element's text in the DevTools Elements panel (double-click, type, Enter) changes the DOM and the page immediately; view source still shows the original.
claims.source_hint: Chrome DevTools docs: Edit the DOM

claims.text: A script can register for a click on an element and, when it happens, create a new p element and insert it after the heading.
The DOM and the HTML source match only until something changes the DOM.

self_check.notes: No code blocks, per DECISIONS.md §3 (2026-09-23): no JS demo file exists and none is added. The Try-it edits the DOM with developer tools instead of a script.
